Frequently Asked Questions

What should I do if I suspect a tree is diseased or dying?

If you suspect a tree is diseased or dying, especially in Chagrin Falls where tree health impacts the local ecosystem and property safety, consult a certified arborist promptly. Early diagnosis can prevent disease spread to other trees and reduce risks from falling limbs. Preparing your property in Chagrin Falls involves clearing the area around the tree, notifying neighbors due to the close-knit community layout, and securing pets and children indoors during removal. Given the town’s historic homes and narrow streets, it’s also important to discuss access and parking with your tree removal service to ensure a smooth and safe operation.

Are there any environmental considerations for tree removal?

Yes, in Chagrin Falls, environmental considerations include protecting native species and wildlife habitats, especially during nesting seasons. Removing invasive species responsibly and planning for replacement planting helps maintain the town’s ecological balance. What happens to the wood after a tree is removed?

Wood from removed trees in Chagrin Falls can be recycled into mulch, firewood, or lumber, supporting local sustainability efforts. Many services, including Roubic Tree and Landscape LLC, offer on-site chipping to create mulch for gardens, helping maintain the town’s natural beauty. Clients can also request to keep wood for personal use.

How often should I have my trees inspected?

Annual inspections are recommended in Chagrin Falls, especially after storms or during seasonal changes, to catch issues early. Regular assessments by certified arborists help maintain tree health, prevent hazards, and preserve the community’s mature tree canopy.
